# Storebot-Google

*Crawler* · also written Storebot

Google's crawler for shopping pages, which checks product pages, prices and checkout for Google Shopping.

**Glossary** (*Storebot-Google*): Google Shopping's own crawler. It crawls more often than Googlebot, goes through product, cart and checkout pages to verify merchant data, and robots.txt rules for it affect all Google Shopping surfaces.

Narrative: the topic [Shopping data: feeds, markup and Storebot](../topics/shopping-data.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

6 claims mention it: 2 from Google's documentation, 3 shown or said at the event (2 confirmed by Google docs, 1 consistent with Google docs), 1 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [About the Google StoreBot crawler](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/13294660?hl=en).

- [`D3-C388`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Docs: Google's Merchant Center help says the StoreBot crawler goes through product detail, cart and checkout pages, can fill in checkout forms, and records price, shipping, availability, coupons and payment methods to verify the data merchants share in Merchant Center. `[D3-C388, docs, Google Merchant Center Help, https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/13294660?hl=en]`
- [`D3-C389`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Docs: Google's crawler list says robots.txt rules addressed to the Storebot-Google user agent affect all surfaces of Google Shopping, such as the Shopping tab in Google Search. `[D3-C389, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-common-crawlers]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D3-C386`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Storebot-Google is used to validate merchant feeds: when a feed gives a price, Google double-checks it on the merchant's site. `[D3-C386, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C387`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Storebot-Google also does deep crawls, for example of checkout pages, which do not belong in the search index; this is another reason it is kept separate from Googlebot. `[D3-C387, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C385`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google Shopping uses its own crawler, Storebot (Storebot-Google), instead of Googlebot because it needs fresh product information, prices, availability and shipping details and therefore crawls much more often. `[D3-C385, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D3-C390`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Analysis: Treat Storebot-Google separately from Googlebot in robots.txt and bot protection: a shop that blocks it on product, cart or checkout paths can undermine Shopping price and availability checks, even when Googlebot is allowed. `[D3-C390, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-SHP-02` **SHOULD** · Documented: Let Storebot-Google crawl product, cart and checkout pages, through robots.txt and bot protection (6 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
